text: Write on-call runbooks for someone half asleep at night, which means exact shell snippets and dashboard links win over long explanations.
Keep build contexts small when touching Dockerfiles, since the remote builder uploads the whole context on every run and large ones time out.
If a stylesheet grows past what one component needs, split the shared parts into `styles/shared/` and leave the page bundle alone.
When adding user-facing strings to the catalog, use the dotted key scheme like `billing.invoice.title` and leave English source text out of the key.
Right-to-left locales get their own visual check whenever a string catalog change touches navigation labels or checkout button text.
Avoid specificity overrides in component CSS, because they break the theme layer that white-label customers depend on for their own branding.
Keep placeholder names in i18n strings descriptive, for example `{customerName}`, and never reuse one key across unrelated screens.
New S3 buckets start with public access blocked, server-side encryption on and a lifecycle rule, all set through the shared storage module.
Verify the signature on inbound payment webhooks before parsing the body, because replayed or forged calls have hit that endpoint before.
New cron schedules go in `ops/crontab.yaml` with an owner and a one-sentence purpose, and they run in UTC.
Give each service its own credential when you set up rotation, and record the consumer list beside it in the rotation ledger.
Mobile builds go through the shared signing pipeline; if you need a new provisioning profile, request it from the mobile group.
Warehouse model changes that alter a published metric need sign-off from the metric's owner, listed in the semantic layer config.
When you add a resolver that calls another service, batch the lookups through the shared data loader and avoid per-item fetches.
Route catalog changes through the translation queue before a locale freeze, since strings added after the freeze ship in English to every market.
Fire purchase analytics events from the server only, since ad blockers silently drop a good share of browser calls and the revenue dashboards drift.
Analytics events use `object_action` names in snake case, such as `invoice_sent`, and every new event needs an entry in the tracking plan.
Statements for public sector customers need tagged PDF output with reading order set, and the accessibility checker has to pass before rollout.
When a PDF export can exceed fifty pages, hand it to the background queue and email the customer a download link.
When a migration touches a table over a few million rows, run the backfill in batches from a background job and not inside the schema change.
Load balancer health check paths should stay cheap; if you change one, confirm the new path does not hit the database.
Helm chart values live in per-environment files under `deploy/values/`; keep the chart defaults safe for a local cluster.
Run containers as the non-root `app` user in any new Dockerfile, because the cluster admission policy rejects pods that start as root.
Do not hardcode account IDs or regions in Terraform resources; read them from the environment's `terraform.tfvars` when a stack needs them.
When rotating secrets, add the new credential first, confirm every consumer picked it up, and only then revoke the old one.
Over-the-air mobile bundles may change only script and asset files; anything that touches native modules has to wait for a store submission.
When adding a field to the search index, state in the mapping file whether it is filterable or only displayed in results.
Secrets rotation for shared service accounts needs a second person on the call and an entry in the rotation ledger.
Do not concatenate translated fragments in the i18n catalog; word order differs across locales, and translators can only work with whole sentences.
When changing CDN cache rules, purge by surrogate key and avoid a full purge outside an active incident on the edge.
If you drop a column in a migration, first confirm no job in the data warehouse still selects it, and then ping the analytics owners.
Cross-region replication on an S3 bucket needs sign-off from the data governance group, who check the residency rules for that region.
Create indexes concurrently in any Postgres migration, since a plain index build takes a lock that has stalled checkout writes before.
If a Dockerfile adds a system package, group it with the existing apt-get install step and clear the apt lists in that same layer.
If Terraform wants to replace a stateful resource, stop and page the infrastructure lead, since a replace on a database wipes the volume.
When you change a Helm chart's templates, run `helm template` against each environment's values and read the rendered diff before rollout.
Use presigned URLs for customer downloads from S3 buckets, because proxying large files through the app servers has exhausted their connection pools.
Keep one Terraform state per environment, because a shared state file once let a staging apply delete production DNS records.
Client-side tracking calls belong in the shared analytics wrapper; page components should not talk to the collector endpoint themselves.
Use table-based layouts in email templates, because several desktop mail clients still ignore flexbox and collapse the design.
New event bus topics need a schema in the registry and a named consuming team before anyone provisions them in production.
Rotate the payment gateway keys in the quiet window on Tuesdays, because the gateway caches credentials and has rejected traffic after a swap.
Evaluate feature flags at the request boundary and pass the result down, since re-evaluating mid-request can give one user two different experiences.
Provider upgrades in Terraform happen one stack at a time, beginning with the sandbox account and ending with production.
Treat iOS entitlements changes as a separate rollout, and confirm the provisioning profile includes them before kicking off a store build.
GraphQL mutations take a single `input` object and hand back a payload with the changed entity and a list of user-facing problems.
When moving objects between S3 buckets, use the batch copy job and check object counts on both sides before removing the source.
When a flag gates billing behavior, get finance sign-off before flipping it above the first rollout cohort of customers.
Inline all CSS in outgoing email templates during the build step, and keep hand-written style attributes out of the source files.
Every cron schedule needs a dead-man check in monitoring, and the alert should page the owning team and not the general rotation.
Do not nest feature flag checks inside other flag checks; if two flags interact, replace them with one combined flag and retire the originals.
If you change a paging schedule, update the rotation table in the on-call runbook the same day and tell the affected engineers directly.
When an incident exposes a missing step, update that service's runbook within the week and link the postmortem at the bottom.
Store screenshots for mobile builds are regenerated by the capture job, so hand-edited images in `store-assets/` get overwritten on the next run.
Add pagination to any new GraphQL list field from the start, because retrofitting connections breaks every client that already queries the field.
Interactive widgets in the web app need keyboard focus states and ARIA labels before the design team approves a new component.
Rotation scripts live in `ops/rotate/`, and any new script there should support a dry run that prints the affected consumers.
Search index mapping changes require a new index and an alias swap; if a reindex runs longer than a shift, hand it over explicitly.
Generate PDF exports in the customer's locale and timezone, since auditors compare the printed dates against their own ledgers.
New foreign keys in migrations should be added with NOT VALID first and validated in a follow-up step during the quiet window.
If a dashboard depends on a sampled event stream, note the sampling rate on the dashboard and avoid combining it with unsampled counts.
Plural forms in the string catalogs use ICU syntax; if a language needs more than two forms, add them all at once.
Database passwords rotate through the secrets manager's scheduled job; do not change one by hand unless that job is broken.
Changes to the GraphQL schema are additive by default; mark a field deprecated and give clients one quarter before removing it.
Subject lines in email templates go through the string catalog, and personalization tags must have a fallback value for blank fields.
Do not put secrets in Helm values; reference the existing sealed secret objects from the chart instead of inlining anything.
Stagger cron jobs that touch the primary database away from the top of the hour, since everything piling up there has caused lock contention.
When editing an email template, preview it in the rendering sandbox at narrow and wide widths before asking marketing to sign off.
If a GraphQL query needs more than three levels of nesting, talk to the API group about a dedicated field first.
Move the minimum OS level in mobile builds only at a planned quarter boundary, and warn users in the app a full cycle ahead.
Do not grant wildcard actions in an S3 bucket policy; list the exact calls the consuming role needs and nothing more.
Size partition counts for a new event bus topic generously at creation, since changing them later reshuffles key ordering for every consumer.
Outbound webhook payloads are additive; if a partner integration needs a breaking shape, publish it under a new event name.
Keep PDF header and footer partials in `pdf/partials/`, and do not copy them into individual export templates.
Do not schedule heavy cron work during the nightly backup window, as the snapshot slows disk writes for everything else on that host.
Android product flavors stay limited to `dev`, `staging` and `prod`; do not add a per-customer flavor without talking to the mobile lead.
New Helm charts must have a liveness probe, a readiness probe and a pod disruption budget before they can go to production.
Flag names use the `team.feature_name` pattern, and kill switches get a `_kill` suffix in the flag dashboard and the config file.
Runbook entries that restart a production service should state how to confirm recovery and who to notify in the ops channel.
New event properties need a described meaning and an allowed value list in the tracking plan before the frontend starts sending them.
When adding a Terraform module, put inputs in `variables.tf` with descriptions and expose only the outputs another stack actually consumes.
Scope every new frontend CSS rule under the component's root class; global selectors belong only in the reset sheet.
When a cron job can overlap with itself, take the advisory lock at startup and exit quietly if another run holds it.
New feature flags go in `flags.yaml` with an owner and a removal date, and default to off in every environment.
Retire a runbook once its alert is gone, because stale on-call pages have sent responders down dead ends during real outages.
Marketing email templates need the unsubscribe partial and the postal address footer, since legal will block the send without them.
Label every new cloud resource in Terraform with `owner` and `cost_center`, using the shared locals block in the stack's root module.
Keep cache lifetimes short on CDN rules for authenticated pages, since a long lifetime once served one customer's dashboard to another.
Run the breaking-change check against registered client queries before publishing the GraphQL schema, since mobile clients in the field update slowly.
Service mesh route changes roll out to a single canary workload first, and the traffic split stays in the mesh config repo.
If a chart adds an ingress, use the shared hostname scheme and ask the network group to allowlist it before the rollout.
New locale files start as a copy of `en.json` with every value empty, and the localization vendor fills them in on their own schedule.
If you move a cron schedule, tell the downstream data owners first and leave the old entry disabled for one full cycle.
Embed fonts in every PDF export template, because some print vendors substitute missing fonts and break the page flow on statements.
Seed data does not belong in schema migrations; put sample rows for staging under `db/seeds/` when a migration needs them.
Do not put email addresses or free text in analytics event properties, because the warehouse copies them to vendors outside our privacy agreement.
Bucket names follow `org-env-purpose`, and anything holding customer data needs a retention note in the storage inventory.
Multi-stage builds go in `deploy/images/`; if you add a new image there, register it in the build matrix in `deploy/images/index.yaml` too.
Percentage rollouts on a feature flag move in steps; wait for one full traffic cycle between steps before widening the cohort.
When editing a Dockerfile, pin the base image by digest rather than a floating label, and keep the final stage free of compilers and package caches.
Field names in the GraphQL schema use camelCase, and enum values use upper snake case, matching the rest of the federated graph.
New component styles should take dark mode colors from the semantic palette variables and leave hex values out of the stylesheet altogether.
Before restoring a production backup into staging, run the anonymization job and confirm customer emails are scrubbed from the copy.
PDF exports render through the headless template service; if you add a new invoice layout, register it in `pdf/templates.yaml` with its page size.
If a credential leaks, treat it as compromised right away: rotate it, check the audit trail, and open an incident even when usage looks clean.
When adding a native dependency to the mobile app, check its binary size impact and record the delta in the build dashboard.
Keep CSS animation to transform and opacity when you touch the marketing pages, as anything else drops frames on the low-end tablets our customers use.
When adding a breakpoint to the CSS, reuse the existing named mixins; a fourth screen size needs sign-off from the design team first.
Remove a feature flag within two sprints of full rollout, since long-lived flags multiply the code paths nobody exercises anymore.
Every new alert needs a linked on-call runbook with the first three diagnostic steps and the escalation contact before it is allowed to page.
Terraform changes run through the shared plan pipeline; apply by hand only during a declared incident and log the change in the incident record.
Set resource requests and limits on every new Helm chart, because the scheduler overpacks nodes and evicts neighbors when they are missing.
Database migrations are forward-only here; if a migration goes wrong, write a new one that repairs the damage instead of editing the old file.
In container entrypoints use exec form, and leave shell wrappers out of production images entirely unless the infrastructure group has signed off on one.
Transactional email templates live in `emails/transactional/`, and any new one needs both an HTML and a plain text body.
Split a column rename into add, backfill and drop steps across separate migrations, because old and new app instances run side by side during rollouts.
When you rename an analytics event, keep firing the old name for one quarter and tell the data team which dashboards depend on it.
In frontend stylesheets, use the spacing tokens from `tokens.css` and skip raw pixel values unless a design spec calls for one explicitly.
Name migration files with the UTC timestamp and a short slug, and keep each file to a single logical schema change.
If a template links to the account area, use the signed link helper and leave raw URLs out of the email entirely.
